import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Read the data
data = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Product distribution (pie chart)
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
product_counts = data['product'].value_counts()
ax1.pie(product_counts.values, labels=product_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90)
ax1.set_title('Product Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 2. Sales by customer age group (bar chart)
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
age_sales = data.groupby('customer_age_group')['total'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
ax2.bar(age_sales.index, age_sales.values, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black')
ax2.set_title('Total Sales by Age Group', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Age Group')
ax2.set_ylabel('Total Sales ($)')
ax2.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 3. Payment method distribution
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
payment_counts = data['payment_method'].value_counts()
ax3.bar(payment_counts.index, payment_counts.values, color=['coral', 'lightgreen'], edgecolor='black')
ax3.set_title('Payment Method Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Payment Method')
ax3.set_ylabel('Count')

# 4. Size distribution
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
size_counts = data['size'].value_counts()
colors_size = ['#ff9999', '#66b3ff', '#99ff99']
ax4.bar(size_counts.index, size_counts.values, color=colors_size, edgecolor='black')
ax4.set_title('Size Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Size')
ax4.set_ylabel('Count')

# 5. Average price by product
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
avg_price = data.groupby('product')['price'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
ax5.barh(avg_price.index, avg_price.values, color='lightcoral', edgecolor='black')
ax5.set_title('Average Price by Product', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Average Price ($)')
ax5.set_ylabel('Product')

# 6. Quantity distribution
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
quantity_counts = data['quantity'].value_counts().sort_index()
ax6.bar(quantity_counts.index, quantity_counts.values, color='plum', edgecolor='black')
ax6.set_title('Quantity Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_xlabel('Quantity')
ax6.set_ylabel('Count')

# 7. Takeaway vs Dine-in
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
takeaway_counts = data['is_takeaway'].value_counts()
labels = ['Takeaway' if x == 1 else 'Dine-in' for x in takeaway_counts.index]
ax7.pie(takeaway_counts.values, labels=labels, autopct='%1.1f%%', colors=['#ff9999', '#66b3ff'], startangle=90)
ax7.set_title('Takeaway vs Dine-in', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 8. Sales over time (hourly)
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1:])
data['hour'] = pd.to_datetime(data['time'], format='%H:%M').dt.hour
hourly_sales = data.groupby('hour')['total'].sum()
ax8.plot(hourly_sales.index, hourly_sales.values, marker='o', linewidth=2, markersize=8, color='darkgreen')
ax8.fill_between(hourly_sales.index, hourly_sales.values, alpha=0.3, color='lightgreen')
ax8.set_title('Total Sales by Hour', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax8.set_xlabel('Hour of Day')
ax8.set_ylabel('Total Sales ($)')
ax8.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
ax8.set_xticks(hourly_sales.index)

# Add overall title
fig.suptitle('Coffee Shop Sales Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)

plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
